subject: Money
title: Prices Always Rise
description: A quick, practical guide to Prices Always Rise.

hook.text: A movie ticket cost $0.25 in 1950. Today it's $11. The movie didn't get better—the dollar got weaker.

buildup.text: Inflation means prices rise over time. The same money buys less. Your grandparents' dollar bought four times more.

discovery.text: Inflation is measured by the Consumer Price Index: a basket of goods tracked monthly by governments.

twist.text: A little inflation is healthy. Central banks target 2% because it encourages spending over hoarding.

climax.text: Zero inflation sounds ideal but causes stagnation. Too much causes chaos. The sweet spot is a gentle rise.

punchline.text: Inflation is the price of a growing economy.

quiz.question: Why do central banks target 2% inflation?
